title: Come to the Living Waters, Come
description: Come to the Living Waters, Come in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 281 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Gospel Invitation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come to the liv-ing wa-ters, come! Glad-ly o-bey your Mak-er's call: Re-turn, ye wea-ry wand'r-ers, home, And find his grace is free for all.

lines: Come to the living waters, come!
And find his grace is free for all.
See from the rock a fountain rise;
For you in healing streams it rolls;
Money ye need not bring, nor price,
In search of empty joys below,
Whither, ah! whither would ye go?
Christ hath the words of endless life.
Your willing ears and hearts incline,
Quicken'd, you then, by faith divine,
A heavenly life on earth shall live.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
